10 units, each with key ideas, worked examples, a 10-mark exam-style question, common mistakes and quick recall

How this book matches your exam. Paper 1 is a guided analysis of unseen non-literary texts:

  • SL: analyse one of two texts; 1 hour 15 minutes; 20 marks; 35%;
  • HL: analyse both texts in separate answers; 2 hours 15 minutes; 40 marks; 35%.

Each text comes with a guiding question that you may use or not. Each answer is marked out of 20:

CriterionMarks
A: Understanding and interpretation5
B: Analysis and evaluation5
C: Coherence, focus and organisation5
D: Language5

All the practice texts in this book are original texts written for StudyStarx, so you can annotate them freely. Check the current guide for the latest details. The mark allocations are our own guides, written in the style of IB markschemes.

Unit 1 of 10: What Paper 1 Asks You to Do

Key ideas

  • Paper 1 assesses how well you analyse how a non-literary text creates meaning for its audience, not just what it says.
  • Non-literary texts include adverts, speeches, opinion columns, blogs, infographics, cartoons, brochures, letters and web pages, among others.
  • The four criteria:
  • A: understanding and interpretation, supported by references;
  • B: analysis and evaluation of the writer's choices (language, structure, visuals) and their effects;
  • C: coherence, focus and organisation;
  • D: language: clear, varied and accurate, in a suitable register.
  • The core skill: feature → effect → purpose. Do not simply spot techniques.

Worked examples

Example 1: a weak point: "The writer uses a rhetorical question."

Example 2: a strong point: "The rhetorical question 'Who will speak for the river?' positions the reader as a possible defender, turning a news story into a personal call to act."

Example 3: an HL timing plan: about 65 minutes per text (10 minutes reading and planning, 50 minutes writing, 5 minutes checking).

10-mark exam-style question

(a) State the length and weighting of Paper 1 for SL and HL. [2]

(b) Explain the difference between identifying and analysing a technique. [4]

(c) Explain how criteria A and B differ. [4]

Answers:

  • (a) SL: 1 h 15 min, 35%; HL: 2 h 15 min, 35% (A2).
  • (b) Identifying names the feature (for example, "a metaphor"); analysing explains how it works, its effect on the reader, and how it serves the text's purpose (R4).
  • (c) Criterion A rewards the overall understanding and a supported interpretation of the text's meaning; Criterion B rewards the close analysis of how the writer's choices shape that meaning, and evaluation of their effectiveness (R4).

Common mistakes

  1. Retelling the text's content.
  2. "Technique spotting" with no effects.
  3. Ignoring the visual features.
  4. Writing with no overall argument.
  5. Spending too long on the first text (HL).

Quick recall

  1. How many texts does an SL student analyse?
  2. How many does an HL student analyse?
  3. How many marks is each answer?
  4. What does Criterion D assess?
  5. What is the core analytical chain?

Answers: 1) One. 2) Two. 3) 20. 4) Language. 5) Feature → effect → purpose.
